title: Drona: Abhimanyu, Ghatotkacha, Drona's death
hook: a young warrior knows how to break into the wheel formation, and says out loud that he doesn't know the way out

segments.voice: Yesterday Drona took command and promised to capture Yudhishthira, if only Arjuna were somewhere else. Your line: Drona: Abhimanyu, Ghatotkacha, Drona's death. Today, Arjuna is somewhere else. Day eight hundred thirty-two.

Morning, and across the field Drona has arranged his army into a shape the Pandavas dread: the chakra, the wheel. Ring inside ring of chariots, elephants and warriors, turning to close around anyone who comes near. On the Pandava side, only a few know how to break it. Arjuna knows. Krishna knows. And Arjuna is far away on the other side of the field, answering the sworn ones' challenge, just as the plan intended. Yudhishthira looks around and finds one more person who might know: Arjuna's son, Abhimanyu. Today, the conversation before he rides in.
screen: `THE WHEEL FORMATION.` → `ARJUNA IS FAR AWAY.` → `ARJUNA'S SON, ABHIMANYU.`

segments.voice: Abhimanyu is the son of Arjuna and Subhadra, Krishna's sister, young and fearless and already a fine warrior. Yudhishthira asks him to break the wheel. Abhimanyu's answer is honest in a way that's hard to read. In Ganguli's telling, he says he knows how to pierce the formation, but if trouble comes, he won't be able to come out again. Some retellings add a story that he learned the way in while still in his mother's womb, hearing it explained, and that she fell asleep before the way out. The epic passage here simply has him say what he knows and what he doesn't. Yudhishthira and Bhima reassure him. You break in, they say, and we'll follow right behind you, through the gap you make. So Abhimanyu drives in. He breaks the ring, and he's inside, fighting brilliantly. But behind him the gap doesn't stay open. Jayadratha, the king of Sindhu, rides into the breach. The text says he once won a gift from Shiva: for one day he could hold back all the Pandavas except Arjuna. This is that day. Bhima, Yudhishthira and the others hurl themselves at the opening and can't get through. The wheel closes. One young man is inside, alone, surrounded by Drona's army. The plan was sound, the courage was real, and one man at the gap undid it.
screen: `ARJUNA'S SON` · `"I KNOW THE WAY IN, NOT OUT"` · `"WE'LL FOLLOW YOU"` · then, large: `JAYADRATHA HOLDS THE GAP`

segments.voice: Sit comfortably and let your feet rest flat. Think of something you're good at starting but not finishing, a project, a conversation, a habit. Breathe in and name the part you know. Breathe out and name, honestly, the part you don't know yet. You don't have to solve it. Just let both be said, the way Abhimanyu said both. If you pray, you can bring that unknown part into your prayer. The bell holds the time.
Drona. Today his wheel formation closes around Arjuna's son, with the gap held shut behind him.
Your line: Drona: Abhimanyu, Ghatotkacha, Drona's death. Today, when you agree to start something, say plainly what you don't know yet, and who will be behind you. Day eight hundred thirty-two.

howItsDone: Abhimanyu's entry into the chakravyuha is told in the Drona Parva of the Mahabharata and is retold in dance, theater and storytelling.

he said plainly he knew the way in, but not the way out.

fork.setup: you're Abhimanyu. you know how to break into the wheel, but not how to get out. your uncles promise to follow you. what do you do?
options: ride in and break it open.
send someone else to try first.
fork.reveal: Abhimanyu rides in and breaks the ring, but Jayadratha closes the gap and the others can't follow.

original.note: the wheel formation: Drona's ring-within-ring battle array.

trapdoor: what you thought: Abhimanyu didn't know enough.
what it means: he told them exactly what he didn't know, and they promised to cover it.
what a scholar hears: the trap isn't only the formation; it's the gap Jayadratha holds, by a boon that works for one day.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Drona Parva (Abhimanyu-vadha Parva), the wheel formation, Abhimanyu's entry and Jayadratha at the breach

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli Abhimanyu's words that he can pierce the array but cannot come out if danger arises, and Yudhishthira and Bhima's promise to follow.

The womb story (hearing the way in from his mother's womb) is labeled as an addition of some retellings; a Keeper should confirm whether Ganguli's text includes any version of it and adjust the myth item if so.
Confirm Jayadratha's boon from Shiva (hold back all Pandavas but Arjuna for one day) as Ganguli tells it.
Abhimanyu's age is deliberately left out.
